notes:
Inbound via self-serve signup (trial credits used). Early discovery with CTO + eng lead. Key context:
- Product: an embeddable in-app chat assistant for mid-market SaaS platforms (billing, project mgmt tools).
- Primary constraint: perceptible latency. Wants streaming token-by-token start within ~150-250ms p50, tail <500ms for first 2 tokens. Overall perceived 'instant' chat UX is their #1 KPI. Quote: "chat must feel like native app — under 300ms or users notice" (CTO).
- Typical convo: short utterances, quick follow-ups. Expect avg turn length 15-40 tokens. Peak concurrency estimate: 30-80 concurrent active users (mostly NA customers).
- Cost sensitivity: SMB budget; looking to keep hosted costs predictable. Interested in Redwood's batching/caching suggestions.
- Model preferences: open/llama-family or compatible models acceptable if streaming & function-calling supported. Want ability to fallback to smaller quantized variant under load.
- Security: SSO (SAML), audit logs for admin console, basic data retention controls; mostly public cloud (no on-prem requirement). SOC2 compliance is buying blocker for some customers.
- PoC status: ran quick POC against Redwood hosted API using streaming endpoint (dev team). Liked latency profile in small test but saw spikes during synthetic load. Wants SE to run latency sweep on real prompt patterns and longer sessions to validate KV-cache behavior.
- Integration notes: Frontend runs in Electron + web (React). They plan to use streaming SSE or websockets. Mentioned existing infra in GCP (us-central1).
- Business: product-led growth with sales-assisted onboarding for >200 seats. If POC passes, likely to move to committed hosted plan. ARR expected to start small and scale with usage.
- Quote from Head of Product during call: "If we can get consistent start-of-stream latency under 250ms at p95, we can roll this out to 10 customers this quarter."
- Internal champion: Lead eng (Marco Ruiz) + Head of Product (Leah Kim). Marco did initial test and left detailed notes in Drive (link above).
- Risks: budget cycle in mid-Apr, SOC2 requirement for enterprise customers may push them to private later; currently prefer Redwood hosted for speed to market.
- Ask: a short, reproducible test plan for latency & streaming behavior; recommended model variants and cost estimates for expected concurrency; guidance on SSE vs websocket best practices.
